ontology.name: FASTO
ontology.scope_summary: FASTO is a FHIR- and SSN-based OWL 2 ontology for type 1 diabetes mobile health clinical decision support. Its intended scope includes integration of real-time WBAN sensor data and historical EHR profile data, personalized treatment plans, insulin regimens, diet, exercise, education, monitoring, temporal reasoning, and semantic interoperability with FHIR, SSN, BFO, and medical terminologies.

competency_questions.question: Can FASTO distinguish hypoglycemia severity levels, especially level 2 and level 3 events, and use those levels to identify when a diabetes treatment plan should be reevaluated?
competency_questions.motivation: Current guidance treats level 2 or 3 hypoglycemia as a clinically important event that should trigger reassessment of the treatment plan. FASTO has hypoglycemia and historical hypoglycemia data, but the current RDF vocabulary does not expose severity-level constructs.

evidence.support: Contains DDO:DDO_0000228 labeled hypoglycemia and FTDM2:hasHistoryOfHypoglycemia on patient, but no local-name or label match for severe hypoglycemia, level 1 hypoglycemia, level 2 hypoglycemia, or level 3 hypoglycemia.

evidence.citation: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes--2026, Section 6, hypoglycemia prevention/treatment discussion and Table 6.7
evidence.support: Official guidance indicates that level 2 or level 3 hypoglycemia should prompt reevaluation of the diabetes treatment plan and possible deintensification within individualized goals.
FASTO identifies emergency handling as a limitation and future extension while current plans focus on insulin regimen, diet, exercise, and education.

suggested_new_entities: level1Hypoglycemia, level2Hypoglycemia, level3Hypoglycemia classes or individuals
competency_questions.sparql_limitation: The query can retrieve patient hypoglycemia history and current care-plan links, but FASTO has no existing severity-level or treatment-plan-reevaluation entity to query without adding vocabulary.
competency_questions.coverage_evidence: The authoritative RDF contains general hypoglycemia and history-of-hypoglycemia modeling but lacks named classes, individuals, properties, or axioms for level 1/2/3 hypoglycemia or severity-triggered plan reevaluation.
competency_questions.related_gap_or_update_need: Add hypoglycemia severity taxonomy and axioms linking level 2/3 hypoglycemia events to review or deintensification of the active care plan.
competency_questions.additional_comment: No external research was used; the question is based only on the supplied ontology, verbalizer, FASTO paper, original competency-question exclusion set, official-source PDFs, and supplied domain-literature PDFs.

competency_questions.question: For patients taking insulin or otherwise at high risk for hypoglycemia, can FASTO represent that glucagon should be prescribed and that family members, caregivers, school personnel, or other support persons should be trained to administer it?
competency_questions.motivation: Glucagon prescribing and support-person training are central to hypoglycemia preparedness, especially for children and people who may rely on others during severe events.

evidence.citation: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes--2026, Recommendation 6.16
evidence.support: Official guidance recommends glucagon for people taking insulin or at high hypoglycemia risk, and education for family, caregivers, school personnel, and other supporters.

Contains patient, hasPatientMedication, Patient.contact, relative, educationRecord, and emergencyLearningTopic, but no caregiver or school-personnel class and no explicit glucagon-prescription/training relation.
FASTO models education plans and personalized treatment plans but identifies emergency handling as an area for extension.

suggested_new_entities: glucagonPrescription object property or medication request specialization
competency_questions.sparql_limitation: The query retrieves insulin-medication, relative/contact, and education-record scaffolding, but cannot test glucagon rescue prescribing or trained caregiver/school-person roles because those constructs are not present in the ontology.
competency_questions.coverage_evidence: FASTO has patient medication, relative/contact, and education-record structures, but lacks the specific rescue-glucagon and support-person training model required by current guidance.
competency_questions.related_gap_or_update_need: Extend emergency-learning and medication-plan modeling with glucagon prescription status, availability/location, and trained support-person roles, including school personnel for children.
competency_questions.additional_comment: No external research was used; the question is based only on the supplied ontology, verbalizer, FASTO paper, original competency-question exclusion set, official-source PDFs, and supplied domain-literature PDFs.

competency_questions.question: Can FASTO classify rescue glucagon formulations by preparation burden and route, such as non-reconstituted glucagon nasal powder, prefilled pen or syringe, dasiglucagon, and powdered glucagon requiring diluent?
competency_questions.motivation: Current official guidance distinguishes ready-to-use glucagon from products requiring reconstitution and prefers non-reconstituted preparations for many emergency users.

evidence.citation: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes--2026, Recommendation 6.16 and Table 6.6
evidence.support: The official source distinguishes glucagon product forms, doses, and preference for preparations that do not need reconstitution.

Contains several glucagon-related classes, but matches are GLP-1 receptor/secretion/resistance concepts rather than rescue glucagon products; no local or label matches for nasal glucagon, dasiglucagon, prefilled glucagon, or reconstitution.
Current literature evaluates low-dose glucagon for exercise-associated hypoglycemia, supporting finer glucagon-product and dose modeling.

PREFIX rdf: <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#>
PREFIX rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>
PREFIX owl: <http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#>

PREFIX ftdm: <https://bioportal.bioontology.org/ontologies/FTDM.owl#>
PREFIX ftdm2: <https://bioportal.bioontology.org/ontologies/FTDM/>
PREFIX fasto: <https://bioportal.bioontology.org/ontologies/FASTO/>
PREFIX fhir: <http://hl7.org/fhir/>
PREFIX ssn: <http://www.w3.org/ns/ssn/>
PREFIX ontofood: <http://www.owl-ontologies.com/OntoFood.owl#>
PREFIX oae: <http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/OAE_>
PREFIX xsd: <http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#>
SELECT ?entity ?label WHERE {
  VALUES ?entity { ftdm:DMTO_0001539 ftdm:DMTO_0001540 ftdm:DMTO_0001541 ftdm:DMTO_0001088 }
  OPTIONAL { ?entity rdfs:label ?label . }
}
competency_questions.sparql_limitation: The query can only expose existing glucagon-labeled vocabulary. It cannot classify rescue formulations or reconstitution burden because those entities and relations are absent.
competency_questions.coverage_evidence: FASTO contains glucagon-adjacent DMTO classes but not the current rescue-product/formulation taxonomy needed for emergency glucagon recommendations.
competency_questions.related_gap_or_update_need: Add a rescue-glucagon formulation hierarchy with route, dose, and reconstitution/preparation attributes aligned to current product categories.
competency_questions.additional_comment: No external research was used; the question is based only on the supplied ontology, verbalizer, FASTO paper, original competency-question exclusion set, official-source PDFs, and supplied domain-literature PDFs.

competency_questions.question: Can FASTO represent the initial treatment protocol for conscious hypoglycemia: fast-acting glucose or carbohydrate, avoidance of high-fat or high-protein foods for initial treatment, glucose recheck after approximately 15 minutes, and repeated treatment if hypoglycemia persists?
competency_questions.motivation: This tests whether FASTO can move from general emergency concepts to a temporal, actionable hypoglycemia-treatment workflow that uses existing nutrition and glucose-monitoring concepts.

evidence.citation: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes--2026, Recommendation 6.15 and hypoglycemia-treatment text
evidence.support: The official source specifies carbohydrate or glucose treatment, rechecking after 15 minutes, repeating treatment if needed, and avoiding high-fat/high-protein foods as initial treatment.
Contains carbohydrate, fat, protein, NutritionOrder, observationValue, and quantity classes/properties, but no temporal protocol or treatment action for conscious hypoglycemia.
The paper states that FASTO did not handle some emergency treatment situations and planned future extension for emergencies.

competency_questions.related_topic: Temporal protocol for treatment of hypoglycemia

competency_questions.related_gap_or_update_need: Model hypoglycemia treatment as a sequence of actions with dose, route, eligibility state, timing, and repeat/seek-care conditions.

competency_questions.question: Can FASTO represent impaired awareness of hypoglycemia, including screening by validated single-question or multi-item tools such as Pedersen-Bjergaard, Gold, Clarke, or HypoA-Q, and link the result to hypoglycemia risk?
competency_questions.motivation: Impaired awareness is a major risk factor for severe hypoglycemia and requires screening and follow-up; it is not equivalent to simply having a history of hypoglycemia.

evidence.citation: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes--2026, impaired awareness discussion
evidence.support: The official source describes impaired awareness, identifies validated tools, and indicates that it increases risk for level 3 hypoglycemia.
Current literature shows impaired awareness and severe hypoglycemia persist in technology users, supporting explicit modeling rather than relying on technology status alone.
Contains hypoglycemia and hasHistoryOfHypoglycemia but no local-name or label match for impaired awareness of hypoglycemia, Gold, Clarke, Pedersen-Bjergaard, or HypoA-Q.

competency_questions.related_topic: Impaired hypoglycemia awareness screening and risk stratification
suggested_new_entities: GoldScore, ClarkeScore, PedersenBjergaardQuestion, HypoAQScore classes or data properties

competency_questions.question: Can FASTO represent fear of hypoglycemia as a psychosocial barrier to achieving glycemic targets and well-being, including a screening question and association with anxiety, depression, hypoglycemia confidence, and HbA1c outcomes?
competency_questions.motivation: Fear of hypoglycemia is clinically distinct from hypoglycemia itself and from impaired awareness; it affects behavior, quality of life, and therapeutic decisions.

evidence.support: The study validates a one-item fear-of-hypoglycemia screening question and reports associations with HbA1c, mental health medication use, and hypoglycemia confidence.

evidence.citation: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes--2026, impaired awareness/prevention discussion
evidence.support: The official source treats fear of hypoglycemia as related to impaired awareness and as relevant to interventions for hypoglycemia prevention.
Contains anxiety and depression classes from imported disease/adverse-event vocabularies, but no fear-of-hypoglycemia or hypoglycemia-confidence entity.

competency_questions.sparql_limitation: The query can retrieve hypoglycemia history and HbA1c goal scaffolding, but cannot test fear-of-hypoglycemia screening, confidence, or psychosocial-barrier semantics because these entities are absent.
competency_questions.coverage_evidence: FASTO contains adjacent clinical and psychosocial entities but no explicit fear-of-hypoglycemia or hypoglycemia-confidence model.
competency_questions.related_gap_or_update_need: Add psychosocial assessment concepts for fear of hypoglycemia, including validated screening responses and links to glycemic targets and behavioral/therapeutic adjustments.

competency_questions.question: Can FASTO represent continuous glucose monitoring metrics such as time in range, time below range, time above range, glucose management indicator, coefficient of variation, and mean glucose, and relate those metrics to individualized glycemic goals?
competency_questions.motivation: Modern glycemic assessment uses CGM metrics alongside A1C, so validation should test whether FASTO can model these derived metrics rather than only raw glucose observations or A1C goals.

evidence.citation: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes--2026, Assessment of Glycemic Status
evidence.support: The official source lists A1C, BGM, and CGM metrics including TIR, TBR, TAR, GMI, coefficient of variation, and mean glucose for glycemic assessment.
Contains observationValue, bloodGlucoseSensor, glucoseSensorOutput, and HbA1c goal entities, but no local-name or label matches for CGM, TIR, TBR, TAR, GMI, or coefficient of variation.

evidence.citation: Journal of Diabetes Science and Technology 2025
evidence.support: Current technology literature evaluates TIR, TBR, TAR, HbA1c, and coefficient of variation as outcomes for advanced hybrid closed-loop systems.

competency_questions.sparql_limitation: The query can retrieve WBAN/sensor scaffolding and HbA1c goals, but FASTO lacks explicit CGM-derived metric classes and goal relations.
competency_questions.coverage_evidence: FASTO models sensor data and HbA1c goals but lacks current CGM metric concepts and individualized CGM-goal axioms.
competency_questions.related_gap_or_update_need: Add derived CGM metric entities and link them to glycemic goal targets, monitoring intervals, and treatment decision criteria.
competency_questions.additional_comment: No external research was used; the question is based only on the supplied ontology, verbalizer, FASTO paper, original competency-question exclusion set, official-source PDFs, and supplied domain-literature PDFs.

competency_questions.question: Can FASTO classify diabetes technology into BGM, CGM, insulin pump or continuous subcutaneous insulin infusion, connected insulin pens, and automated insulin delivery systems, including the relation by which AID uses CGM-informed algorithms to modulate insulin delivery?
competency_questions.motivation: FASTO's original sensor model predates the current centrality of AID systems and connected insulin devices in diabetes technology recommendations.

evidence.citation: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes--2026, Diabetes Technology introduction and general device principles
evidence.support: The official source defines technology categories including BGM, CGM, insulin administration devices, AID systems, connected insulin pens, and software medical devices.

Contains SSN sensor, WBAN, bloodGlucoseSensor, glucoseSensorOutput, and device classes, but no matches for CGM, AID, automated insulin delivery, connected insulin pen, insulin pump, or hybrid closed loop.
FASTO integrates WBAN sensor readings and FHIR/SSN for real-time monitoring but does not enumerate modern AID technology categories.

competency_questions.sparql_query:
PREFIX rdf: <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#>
PREFIX rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>
PREFIX owl: <http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#>

competency_questions.coverage_evidence: FASTO covers generic sensors and WBAN integration but not the current device taxonomy or AID-specific relations.
competency_questions.related_gap_or_update_need: Add an explicit diabetes-technology module aligned with current BGM, CGM, pump/CSII, connected pen, AID, and software medical-device terminology.

competency_questions.question: Can FASTO represent advanced hybrid closed-loop system use and its real-world outcome profile, including TIR/TBR changes, severe hypoglycemia, ketoacidosis, skin/adhesive problems, practical barriers, and treatment satisfaction?
competency_questions.motivation: Current clinical literature evaluates AID/AHCL systems using safety, patient-reported outcomes, and CGM metrics, not just medication or sensor readings.

evidence.citation: Journal of Diabetes Science and Technology 2025, abstract/results
evidence.support: The study evaluates advanced hybrid closed-loop systems using HbA1c, TIR, TBR, severe hypoglycemia, ketoacidosis, skin problems, practical barriers, and treatment satisfaction.
The study reports persistent severe hypoglycemia and impaired awareness despite high use of CGM and AID, supporting ongoing surveillance of risk even with technology.
No local-name or label matches were found for advanced hybrid closed-loop, hybrid closed loop, automated insulin delivery, treatment satisfaction, or skin adhesive problems.

competency_questions.sparql_limitation: No faithful SPARQL query can be written without inventing AHCL/AID, patient-reported-outcome, and safety-outcome entities; querying only generic device or sensor classes would not test the intended competency.
competency_questions.coverage_evidence: FASTO lacks AHCL/AID device-use vocabulary and outcome constructs for patient-reported satisfaction, practical barriers, skin/adhesive problems, and CGM-derived safety metrics.
competency_questions.related_gap_or_update_need: Add technology-use episodes and outcome/safety assessment patterns for AID/AHCL systems, including CGM metrics and patient-reported outcomes.

competency_questions.question: Can FASTO model mealtime insulin adjustment using carbohydrate intake together with fat and protein intake, concurrent glycemia, glycemic trends, sick-day management, and anticipated physical activity?
competency_questions.motivation: FASTO already includes carbohydrate ratios and real-time insulin adjustment, but current guidance includes additional dose-modifying factors that are not reducible to carbohydrate grams alone.

evidence.citation: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes--2026, Recommendation 9.3
evidence.support: The official source states that people with type 1 diabetes should learn to match mealtime insulin to carbohydrate and fat/protein intake and modify correction doses based on glycemia, trends, sick days, and anticipated activity.
The paper notes that FASTO diet plans are based on carbohydrate grams and that proteins and fats need a clearer role in meal planning.
Contains insulinToCarbohydrateRatio, carbohydrate, fat, protein, exercisePlan, and insulin-regimen entities; no local-name or label matches for sick-day management or glycemic trends.

competency_questions.related_topic: Mealtime insulin dosing factors beyond carbohydrate counting
competency_questions.sparql_limitation: The query retrieves carbohydrate-ratio and exercise-plan scaffolding, but cannot represent fat/protein dose modifiers, glycemic trends, sick-day context, or correction-dose logic without new entities and rules.
competency_questions.coverage_evidence: FASTO covers carbohydrate-based dose support and exercise context, but current guidance requires dose factors that are either absent or under-modeled.
competency_questions.related_gap_or_update_need: Extend insulin-dosing rules with fat/protein intake, trend-aware CGM data, sick-day contexts, and anticipated activity modifiers.

competency_questions.question: Can FASTO distinguish insulin-delivery treatment modalities for adults with type 1 diabetes, including continuous subcutaneous insulin infusion, multiple daily injections of basal and prandial insulin, inhaled insulin, and the distinction between insulin analogs and human insulin?

evidence.support: The official source recommends CSII or multiple daily doses of prandial and basal insulin for most adults with type 1 diabetes and prefers insulin analogs or inhaled insulin over injectable human insulin to minimize hypoglycemia risk.

evidence.citation: Original CQs Q6, Q8, Q10, Q17
evidence.support: Original questions cover current regimen and selected insulin ingredients, but not delivery-modality taxonomy or analog/human/inhaled classification.

competency_questions.sparql_limitation: The query retrieves insulin-regimen structure, but FASTO cannot classify CSII, MDI, inhaled insulin, analog insulin, or human insulin without additional modality and insulin-class vocabulary.
competency_questions.coverage_evidence: The ontology covers insulin regimens and basal/bolus components but under-models current delivery modalities and analog/human/inhaled distinctions.

evidence.support: The official source recommends regular reevaluation of insulin treatment plans and behaviors, for example every 3 to 6 months, to incorporate factors affecting treatment choice and goals.

evidence.citation: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes--2026, Children and Adolescents introduction
evidence.support: The official source states that guidance is provided for transition from pediatric to adult diabetes care to ensure continued care.

Contains child, adolescent, adult, carePlan, EpisodeOfCare.patient, Encounter, and educationRecord-related entities, but no local-name or label match for transition-to-adult-care, transition readiness, transfer, or continuity plan.
FASTO supports long-term and real-time treatment plans, but the paper does not describe a pediatric-to-adult transition model.

competency_questions.question: For older adults with diabetes, can FASTO represent geriatric syndromes and related risks--such as cognitive impairment, depression, falls, frailty, persistent pain, urinary incontinence, hypoglycemia, and polypharmacy--and use them to individualize goals and therapeutic approaches?
competency_questions.motivation: Older-adult care requires multidomain assessment and goal individualization. FASTO has oldAdult and some disease terms, but not the full geriatric-syndrome/risk pattern.

evidence.citation: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes--2026, Recommendations 13.1 and 13.2
evidence.support: The official source recommends comprehensive medical, psychological, functional, and social assessment and annual screening for geriatric syndromes, hypoglycemia, and polypharmacy.

evidence.citation: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes--2026, hypoglycemia and CGM discussion
evidence.support: The official source also emphasizes querying older adults and care partners about hypoglycemia history, impaired awareness, and fear of hypoglycemia.

Contains oldAdult, depression, hypoglycemia, patientProfile, carePlan, and socialHistory, but no local-name or label matches for frailty, falls, polypharmacy, geriatric syndrome, or cognitive impairment.

competency_questions.related_topic: Older-adult multidomain assessment and individualized care

competency_questions.coverage_evidence: FASTO has older-adult and generic clinical scaffolding, but does not model the geriatric-syndrome set or its effect on goals and therapies.
competency_questions.related_gap_or_update_need: Add geriatric assessment, frailty/cognitive/fall/polypharmacy concepts, and rules linking those assessments to goal and therapy individualization.

competency_questions.motivation: FASTO includes some patient preference and social-history scaffolding, but current care recommendations require broader social and economic context for shared decision-making and safety.

competency_questions.question: Can FASTO represent dietary patterns and evidence strength for type 1 diabetes management--such as high-fiber diets and carbohydrate-restricted diets--and link them to outcomes including HbA1c, TIR, coefficient of variation, hypoglycemia, insulin dose, and anthropometric measures?
competency_questions.motivation: FASTO's original diet model is centered on carbohydrate grams, while current evidence evaluates broader dietary patterns and multi-metric outcomes.

evidence.support: The current review synthesizes RCT evidence on dietary patterns in type 1 diabetes, including high-fiber and carbohydrate-restricted diets and outcomes such as HbA1c, TIR, CV, hypoglycemia, insulin dose, and body measures.
The paper reports that FASTO diet plans are based on carbohydrate grams and notes future needs for protein/fat roles, familiar/preferred foods, and measurement units.

Contains carbohydrate, Fiber, fat, protein, has_fiber, hasFatsPerGramOfFood, has_protein_per_food, NutritionOrder, and dailyCalories, but no dietary-pattern or evidence-certainty/outcome model for RCT findings.

competency_questions.related_topic: Dietary pattern evidence and multi-outcome nutrition modeling
competency_questions.sparql_query:
PREFIX rdf: <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#>
PREFIX rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>
PREFIX owl: <http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#>
PREFIX ddo: <http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/DDO.owl#>
PREFIX ftdm: <https://bioportal.bioontology.org/ontologies/FTDM.owl#>
PREFIX ftdm2: <https://bioportal.bioontology.org/ontologies/FTDM/>
PREFIX fasto: <https://bioportal.bioontology.org/ontologies/FASTO/>
PREFIX fhir: <http://hl7.org/fhir/>
PREFIX ssn: <http://www.w3.org/ns/ssn/>
PREFIX ontofood: <http://www.owl-ontologies.com/OntoFood.owl#>
PREFIX oae: <http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/OAE_>
PREFIX xsd: <http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#>
SELECT ?diet ?dailyCalories ?nutrient ?amount WHERE {
  ?diet rdf:type fhir:nutritionOrder .
  OPTIONAL { ?diet fasto:NutritionOrder.dailyCalories ?dailyCalories . }
  OPTIONAL {
    ?diet <http://hl7.org/fhir/NutritionOrder.oralDiet> ?oralDiet .
    ?oralDiet <http://hl7.org/fhir/NutritionOrder.oralDiet.nutrient> ?nutrient .
    OPTIONAL { ?nutrient <http://hl7.org/fhir/NutritionOrder.oralDiet.nutrient.amount> ?amount . }
  }
}
competency_questions.sparql_limitation: The query retrieves nutrition-order nutrient scaffolding, but dietary pattern categories, evidence certainty, and outcome links to CGM metrics or insulin-dose outcomes are not modeled.
competency_questions.coverage_evidence: FASTO has nutrient and nutrition-order modeling, but not evidence-based dietary-pattern/outcome modeling for current type 1 diabetes nutrition literature.
competency_questions.related_gap_or_update_need: Extend the diet module with dietary-pattern classes, evidence-strength annotations, and outcome relations including CGM metrics, insulin dose, hypoglycemia, and anthropometrics.
competency_questions.additional_comment: No external research was used; the question is based only on the supplied ontology, verbalizer, FASTO paper, original competency-question exclusion set, official-source PDFs, and supplied domain-literature PDFs.
